title: India refrains from reacting to Bangladesh PM Rahman's allegations over protests

ai.summary: India declined to comment on Bangladesh PM Rahman's allegations that Awami League is orchestrating protests across the border, stating the protests are an internal issue of Bangladesh and emphasizing desire for positive bilateral relations.

facts.claim: India declined to comment on Bangladesh PM Rahman's allegations that Awami League is orchestrating protests across the border
facts.quote: India on Friday declined to comment on Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's allegations that the Awami League is orchestrating the ongoing protests at the behest of its masters "across the border," reported PTI.

facts.claim: India stated the protests are an internal issue of Bangladesh
facts.quote: New Delhi said the protests are an internal issue of Bangladesh and that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with that country.

facts.claim: India emphasized desire for positive bilateral relations with Bangladesh
facts.quote: Our position remains consistent-- that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh, one which is rooted in the shared histories of the two countries and in their shared cultural ties of their peoples," he said, reported PTI.

ai.background_note: Bangladesh's former leader Sheikh Hasina has been living in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 following violent student-led protests.
